purpose: Structures the Role A answer for downstream mapping WITHOUT interpreting it. The transcriber records what the respondent said, verbatim where possible, and marks every item the respondent did not settle.
hard_rules: The raw response is preserved byte-for-byte and hashed BEFORE this schema is populated. This schema is a derived view, never a replacement.
The transcriber may not supply, complete, tidy, or infer any field the respondent left unsettled. 'unsettled' is a valid and expected value.
The transcriber may not translate the respondent's vocabulary into any other framework's vocabulary. Terms are recorded as the respondent used them.
If the transcriber believes a field is implied but not stated, it is recorded as unsettled with the belief noted in transcriber_observations, never promoted into the field.

scope_A.note: System classes in scope and excluded, in the respondent's own words.

observables_B.note: Facts or behaviours the respondent says matter.

carryover_D.note: The respondent's own definition of what carrying over means.

comparison_H.note: Whether the respondent offers any way to compare competing answers, and what they say makes it natural. THIS FIELD IS LOAD-BEARING: it is the respondent's own comparison criterion, and the adjudication procedure privileges it over any project-supplied criterion.

transcriber_observations.note: Anything the transcriber noticed that is NOT part of the answer. Never feeds a field above.

optional_architecture_phase.gate: Populated only after every field above is frozen and hashed, and still BEFORE any reveal.
optional_architecture_phase.question_asked: Given the answer you have just finalised, what minimal or canonical way of structuring such a description, if any, follows from it? Concluding that none follows, or that several do, is an acceptable answer.

derivation_from_own_contract.note: How the respondent says it follows from their own answer above.

optional_architecture_phase.separation_rule: This is a SECOND frozen artifact with its own hash. Contract-to-contract and architecture-to-architecture comparisons are reported separately and are never collapsed into a single agreement score.
